content:
maria: Heads-up — customer reported unexpected provisional charges after a canary routing fallback yesterday. looks like toolcall retries + prefetch heartbeat overlaps created a 'shadow' billing window where tokens were counted twice.
kevin: ugh. any traces/ids?
maria: sent the session id in DMs but summary here: session=svc-8371, route switched host -> fallback at 14:03:12, client retried, prefetch sidecar had TTL overlap and sent a midstream toolcall that got truncated then replayed. console shows provisional_charge spikes for that session.
dana: do we have the metric that separates provisional vs confirmed token commits? iirc we stamp provisional at prefetch, then confirm on final ack.
kevin: we do: billing.provisional.tokens and billing.confirmed.tokens. problem is the router's grace-window (-> 500ms) allowed a second ephemeral path to claim ownership and emit provisional tokens before original lease expired. race condition.
ops-bot: [alert] provisional-charge-spike svc-8371 (14:03) count=128 provisional_tokens, confirmed_tokens=64 :eyes:
maria: exact. so customer sees +64 tokens effectively shadowed until reconciliation. reconciliation runs daily, but SLA says we should avoid visible spikes in the console/alerts. UX picked up the provisional numbers and alerted on them.
kevin: options: 1) tighten grace-window (risky for flapping), 2) dedupe provisional claims at router-level by session id + nonce, 3) change console/alerting to ignore provisional unless confirmed within Xs.
dana: +3. change UX is fastest short-term. show provisional but mark as "pending" and exclude from alerting thresholds. long-term we should prevent double provisional claim.
maria: agreed. but also need telemetry so we can root-cause faster. can we add a trace tag when a provisional token is emitted that says "claim_origin=router:<host>" and a claim_nonce?
kevin: yes. we can emit tags in billing events: claim_origin, claim_nonce, prior_owner. then our reconcile job can detect duplicate nonces and suppress later provisional increments.
dana: will need a tiny console change to surface claim_origin in the per-session view + a filter in the graph. I can do the frontend part.
kevin: backend: PR incoming to router to attach nonce to provisional ledger entries and to the prefetch sidecar so the heartbeat includes it. also add dedupe check in provisional ingest module. quick pseudo-SQL to find dupes:
```
SELECT claim_nonce, COUNT(*) as cnt, SUM(provisional_tokens) as tokens
FROM billing_events
WHERE event_time BETWEEN '2026-03-21T14:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-21T15:00:00Z'
AND session_id = 'svc-8371'
GROUP BY claim_nonce
HAVING cnt > 1;
```
maria: perfect. can we also add an internal api to query provisional vs confirmed per-route for the last 1h for alerts? very handy for on-call.
kevin: yep, adding /internal/metrics/session_provisional?session=svc-8371&window=1h returning JSON with provenance fields. I'll stick a small rate-limit.
ops-bot: [deploybot] router-provisional-nonce-flag deployed to canary at 17:02 :thumbsup:
dana: I'll land the console patch to hide provisional from alerting and add the small provenance column in the session modal.
maria: owners: kevin (router + ingestion dedupe) + dana (console UX). i'll open a runbook note for oncall: "provisional spike -> check claim_nonce duplicates -> hit /internal/metrics -> run reconcile if needed".
kevin: timeline: hotfix UX change today, dedupe change to router + ingestion early next week.
maria: thanks. filing follow-up tickets and adding to the rollout checklist (canary -> opt-in demo orgs -> global). :sparkles:
